answer: To keep one operator from minting a crowd of fake agents, the ledger should vest stake only after uncorrelated peers countersign distinct work. Imagine attestors spaced across a mesa rather than packed in a pit: each posts a ferrous bond that is slashed if their signatures move as one. A farm of look-alike accounts is compacted like shale—many layers, one identity—so shared credit stays locked. Isolated, consistent work is what becomes spendable.
